Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S3, S4

As a PR author, I want to pick several suggestions and apply them together so that my branch gets
one commit instead of one per suggestion.

### User Scenario

Ana leaves four suggestions on two files. Ben clicks **Add to batch** on three of them; a bar at the
bottom shows "3 suggestions selected · Apply". He applies them and the PR gets one commit changing
both files, and all three comments are marked applied.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given several selected suggestions, when applied, then one commit containing all of
    them is added and each is marked applied (S4) with that commit.
*    AC2: Given two selected suggestions whose lines overlap, when the user tries to add the second
    to the batch, then it is refused with "overlaps another suggestion in this batch".
*    AC3: Given one suggestion in the batch is outdated, when applied, then nothing is committed
    and the outdated one is named (all or nothing).
*    AC4: Given the batch is left unapplied and the page is reloaded, then the batch is empty (it
    is not stored server-side).
*    AC5: Permission, closed/merged PR and stale head rules are the same as S3.

### Out of Scope

*   Batches across PRs; saving a batch for later.

### Open Questions

*   Is there a maximum batch size? (Proposed: 50.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's service to take a list of comment IDs and build one
`ChangeRepoFiles` call with one entry per file, applying edits in a file bottom-up so earlier
replacements don't shift later line numbers.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Apply each suggestion as its own commit in a loop._ Easy, but not atomic: a failure halfway
    leaves a partial result, and it is not what the user asked for.
*   _Store pending batches server-side._ Survives reloads, but needs a table and cleanup for
    something the user does in one sitting.

**Rationale:** One `ChangeRepoFiles` call is a single atomic commit, and bottom-up edits are a
simple, testable way to avoid line drift.

**Consequences:** S3's function signature changes; S7's batch endpoint reuses it.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches a few different components

    Spec reviewed — [@controlled-opposition](https://github.com/controlled-opposition)

    **Acceptance criteria:**

    *   AC1: testable. One commit, all suggestions marked applied with that commit.
    *   AC2: testable. The refusal message is exact.
    *   AC3: testable. All or nothing, and the outdated one is named.
    *   AC4: testable by reloading the page, but state how the test checks it (a UI or E2E check, since there is no server state to assert).
    *   AC5: "same as S3" sends the reader to another issue and bundles three rules (permission, closed or merged PR, stale head). Please state each, ideally one AC per rule with its expected response.

    **Cases considered:**

    *   Covered: several suggestions, overlap, one outdated suggestion, reload.
    *   Not covered by any AC: two suggestions in one file that change line counts differently (the design relies on bottom-up edits to avoid line drift, but no AC tests it), a suggestion that was already applied, a batch of one, an empty batch (is Apply hidden or disabled?), the same suggestion added twice, and a batch larger than the maximum (the Open Question proposes 50 but no AC enforces it).
    *   The overlap check (AC2) needs ranges, so the issue depends on S5 ([S5. Suggest a change across several lines #158](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/158)) as well as S3 and S4.

    **Scope:**

    *   The justification ("Touches a few different components") is a fragment. Please name the components and give the one or two sentences of why.
    *   Medium fits: one service change, one UI bar, one commit.
    *   Name the dependencies by number: S3 ([S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch #156](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/156)), S4 ([S4. Record and show that a suggestion was applied #157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/157)), S5 ([S5. Suggest a change across several lines #158](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/158)).

    **Other:**

    *   The Design Decision names two alternatives and a reason, which meets D3.
    *   The issue was not on the `Sprint 3` milestone; I have added it.

    **Verdict:** Changes needed: make AC5 explicit, add the line-drift and already-applied cases, resolve the batch-size question, add the S5 dependency, fix the scope justification.

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on S3, S4

As a PR author, I want to pick several suggestions and apply them together so that my branch gets
one commit instead of one per suggestion.

### User Scenario

Ana leaves four suggestions on two files. Ben clicks **Add to batch** on three of them; a bar at the
bottom shows "3 suggestions selected · Apply". He applies them and the PR gets one commit changing
both files, and all three comments are marked applied.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given several selected suggestions, when applied, then one commit containing all of
  them is added and each is marked applied (S4) with that commit.
- [ ] AC2: Given two selected suggestions whose lines overlap, when the user tries to add the second
  to the batch, then it is refused with "overlaps another suggestion in this batch".
- [ ] AC3: Given one suggestion in the batch is outdated, when applied, then nothing is committed
  and the outdated one is named (all or nothing).
- [ ] AC4: Given the batch is left unapplied and the page is reloaded, then the batch is empty (it
  is not stored server-side).
- [ ] AC5: Permission, closed/merged PR and stale head rules are the same as S3.

### Out of Scope

- Batches across PRs; saving a batch for later.


### Open Questions

- Is there a maximum batch size? (Proposed: 50.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's service to take a list of comment IDs and build one
`ChangeRepoFiles` call with one entry per file, applying edits in a file bottom-up so earlier
replacements don't shift later line numbers.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply each suggestion as its own commit in a loop.* Easy, but not atomic: a failure halfway
  leaves a partial result, and it is not what the user asked for.
- *Store pending batches server-side.* Survives reloads, but needs a table and cleanup for
  something the user does in one sitting.

**Rationale:** One `ChangeRepoFiles` call is a single atomic commit, and bottom-up edits are a
simple, testable way to avoid line drift.

**Consequences:** S3's function signature changes; S7's batch endpoint reuses it.


### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches a few different components
======

- AC5: "same as S3" sends the reader to another issue and bundles three rules (permission, closed or merged PR, stale head). Please state each, ideally one AC per rule with its expected response.

## User Story
As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion with one click so that Gitea commits the
change to my branch and I don't retype it.

### User Scenario

Ben sees Ana's suggestion and clicks **Apply suggestion**. A small form shows a default commit
message, "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go", which he keeps. He confirms. The page reloads,
the PR has one more commit changing line 18, and the Files tab shows the new code.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with
the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on a single line, in a review comment or a reply in its thread, and
  a user who can push to the head branch, when they apply it, then exactly one commit is added to
  the head branch that replaces only that line, exactly as #154's diff shows it (AC12). The form
  is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>" and can be
  edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted
  empty.
- [ ] AC2: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
  "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
  direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply

  on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*

  suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number

7	## User Story
8	As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion with one click so that Gitea commits the
9	change to my branch and I don't retype it.
10
11	### User Scenario
12
13	Ben sees Ana's suggestion and clicks **Apply suggestion**. A small form shows a default commit
14	message, "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go", which he keeps. He confirms. The page reloads,
15	the PR has one more commit changing line 18, and the Files tab shows the new code.
16
17	### Acceptance Criteria
18
19	Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with
20	the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise.
21
22	- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on a single line, in a review comment or a reply in its thread, and
23	  a user who can push to the head branch, when they apply it, then exactly one commit is added to
24	  the head branch that replaces only that line, exactly as #154's diff shows it (AC12). The form
25	  is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>" and can be
26	  edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted
27	  empty.
28	- [ ] AC2: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
29	  "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
30	  direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply
31	  button, and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing. *Pending customer question 2
32	  on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
33	- [ ] AC3: Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the
34	  suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number
35	  is now past the end of the file, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see
36	  "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
37	- [ ] AC4: Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another
38	  suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is
39	  committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page
40	  and try again." This holds whether or not the new commits touched the suggestion's file. The
41	  head SHA sent is the PR's head when the page loaded, even when the Files tab is showing a single
42	  earlier commit.
43	- [ ] AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, its head branch was deleted, or it was created with
44	  AGit flow (so it has no head branch), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST commits nothing and returns 400 with
45	  "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists."
46	- [ ] AC6: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when they apply, then
47	  nothing is committed and they see Gitea's existing message `Cannot commit to protected branch
48	  "<branch>".` (the same check and text as the web editor), not the raw pre-receive output.
49	- [ ] AC7: Given a comment with zero or several suggestion blocks, or a comment on an old-side
50	  (deleted) line, which #154 AC7 renders as an ordinary code block, when shown, then there is no
51	  Apply button.
52	- [ ] AC8: The commit's author and committer follow the customer's answer to question 1, and a
53	  test asserts them. *Pending customer question 1 on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
54	- [ ] AC9: Given an outdated review comment (its code changed in a later push), when shown, then
55	  its suggestion has no Apply button. A POST from a page loaded before the change is handled by
56	  AC3/AC4.
57	- [ ] AC10: Given a suggestion identical to the current line, when someone applies it, then no
58	  commit is made and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code."
59	- [ ] AC11: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, when a suggestion on it is
60	  applied, then the changed line keeps the file's line ending and the file's final-newline state
61	  is unchanged; no other byte of the file changes.
62	- [ ] AC12: Given the suggestion block is empty, has one blank line, or has several lines, when it

66	### Out of Scope
67
68	- Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).
69	- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines (customer question 5): they render as plain code blocks
70	  in #154, so there is nothing to apply. If the customer allows them, that's a follow-up issue.

92	### Design Decision
93
94	**Decision:** A new `ApplySuggestion(ctx, doer, comment, expectedHeadSHA, message)` in
95	`services/repository/files`, next to `ChangeRepoFiles`, that first checks that `expectedHeadSHA` is
96	still the head branch's commit (AC4) and that the doer may commit to the branch, using the same
97	protected-branch check the web editor builds its `CanCommitToBranch` from
98	(`GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule` and `CanUserPush`; AC6). It then reads the file at the current head, checks the target line still matches
99	`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` from #154 (ignoring a trailing `\r` on both sides, so CRLF files
100	compare correctly), replaces it with the block's lines, and commits through
101	`ChangeRepoFiles` with
102	`LastCommitID = expectedHeadSHA`. Permission is checked with the same head-branch write check the
103	web editor uses for PR branches, including `AllowMaintainerEdit`.
104
105	**Alternatives Considered:**
106	- *Apply with `git apply` on a patch built from the suggestion, in a temporary clone.* Handles
107	  fuzz, but fuzzy application can land the change on the wrong line, and it duplicates what
108	  `ChangeRepoFiles` already does (temp repo, hooks, protection checks, push).
109	- *Just replace line N without comparing contents.* Simple, but silently overwrites code if the
110	  file changed since the review (AC3).
111	- *Rely on `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check alone for AC4.* That check only fails when the
112	  same file changed since `LastCommitID` (`services/repository/files/update.go:393`). If another
113	  file changed, it commits on the stale parent and the push is rejected as out of date, which the
114	  web editor reports with its generic "file contents have changed" message, not AC4's.
115	- *Put `ApplySuggestion` in `services/pull` (this decision's first version).* `services/repository/files`
116	  already imports `services/pull` (`update.go`, `cherry_pick.go`), so `services/pull` calling
117	  `ChangeRepoFiles` would be an import cycle, which Go does not allow.
118
119	**Rationale:** `ChangeRepoFiles` already runs hooks, re-checks branch protection on push and
120	handles the temp repo, so only the suggestion-specific checks are new. Checking the head SHA and
121	`CanCommitToBranch` up front gives AC4 and AC6 their own messages instead of whatever the push
122	returns. Comparing line contents makes outdated suggestions fail safe.
123
124	**Consequences:** Applying a suggestion triggers the normal push path (CI, PR recheck,
125	`InvalidateCodeComments`). A suggestion whose line moved but didn't change is refused rather than
126	re-located; a later issue could add re-anchoring. Any push to the branch, even one unrelated to
127	the suggestion's file, makes an open page's Apply fail with AC4 until it is reloaded.
128
129	### Decision 2: reading suggestion blocks on the server
130
131	**Decision:** Add `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in `models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`, next to
132	#154's `SuggestionOriginalLine()`. It parses `Comment.Content` with Gitea's own goldmark markdown
133	parser and returns the text of each fenced code block whose first info word is exactly
134	`suggestion`. The Apply POST reads the suggested text from it (the client never sends the text),
135	and AC7's "exactly one block" rule counts with it. S4 and S6 can reuse it.
136
137	**Alternatives Considered:**
138	- *A line scanner or regex over the raw markdown.* Simpler and faster, but it can disagree with
139	  the rendered page on fences inside lists or blockquotes, `~~~` fences, longer fences and info
140	  strings (#154 AC9), so Apply could commit something other than the diff on screen.
141	- *Have the browser send the suggestion text with the POST.* No parser needed, but the commit would
142	  hold whatever the request says rather than what the comment says.
143
144	**Rationale:** Only goldmark is guaranteed to find the same blocks the page renders, so what the
145	reader sees is what gets committed.
146
147	**Consequences:** Parsing the comment costs a markdown parse per Apply and per comment shown with
148	an Apply button. The parser lives in the model package and must be kept in step with any future
149	change to how #154 recognises suggestion blocks.
150
151	### Decision 3: where the Apply button comes from
152
153	**Decision:** The server adds a `data-suggestion-apply-url` attribute and the PR's head SHA next to
154	#154's `data-suggestion-original` on the comment body, only when this viewer may apply (AC2, AC5,
155	AC9; old-side comments already get no attribute, AC7). #154's `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`
156	then adds the Apply button and commit-message form to the diff header when the comment has
157	exactly one suggestion block. The server re-checks every condition on POST.
158
159	**Alternatives Considered:**
160	- *Render the button in `repo/diff/comments.tmpl` and `conversation.tmpl`, outside the markup.*
161	  Works without JavaScript, but the server would need to parse every comment at render time to
162	  count blocks, and the button would sit apart from the diff it applies, laid out twice.
163	- *A separate frontend handler that finds #154's rendered diffs.* Keeps #154's file untouched, but
164	  depends on its generated markup and runs as a second pass over the same comments.
165
166	**Rationale:** It follows #154's own design (the server supplies data attributes, the browser
167	draws the suggestion), covers both tabs with one code path, and re-renders after a comment is
168	edited (#154 AC8).
169
170	**Consequences:** No JavaScript means no button (Out of Scope). Changes to `suggestion.ts` must
171	keep #154's tests passing, and S4's "applied" marker will probably go in the same header.
172

179	One new service function in `services/repository/files` and a goldmark-based `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in
180	`models/issues`, both with unit tests; one web route and handler with the permission and PR-state
181	checks; two data attributes in #154's two comment templates; the Apply button and commit-message
182	form in #154's `suggestion.ts` with Vitest tests; a few locale strings; and integration tests for
183	the permission and error cases (AC2, AC4–AC6) sharing one PR setup to keep them fast. No schema
184	change. Recording the applied state is S4.

203	## Part 1: issue body
204
205	### User Story
206
207	Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #156 (S3, merged in #179)
208
209	As a reviewer, I want to see which of my suggestions were applied, by whom and in which commit,
210	so that I don't re-check feedback that is already handled.
211
212	### User Scenario
213
214	Ben applies Ana's suggestion on line 18 of `main.go`. The page reloads. In the suggestion's
215	header, Ana's comment now shows "Applied by @ben in `a1b2c3d4e5`" with a link to the commit, and
216	the Apply button is gone. The comment is also marked Outdated, as any comment on a changed line
217	is. The timeline shows Gitea's usual "ben added 1 commit" entry, with the message "Apply
218	suggestion from @ana on main.go".
219
220	### Acceptance Criteria
221
222	The marker is drawn by #154's `suggestion.ts`, like the Apply button. Without JavaScript the
223	suggestion is a plain code block with no marker, as in #154 and #156.
224
225	- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion was applied, when its comment is shown, then the suggestion's header
226	  shows "Applied by @<applier> in <short SHA>" and has no Apply button. The short SHA is Gitea's
227	  usual 10 characters, linked to `<base repo>/commit/<full SHA>`. This holds in the Conversation
228	  tab and in the Files tab whenever outdated comments are shown (the default). It holds for every
229	  viewer who can see the comment: signed out, without push access, and on a closed or merged PR.
230	- [ ] AC2: Given an applied suggestion, when anyone POSTs Apply for it again, then nothing is
231	  committed and the response is 400 with "This suggestion has already been applied." This check
232	  runs right after S3's 404 checks (not applicable, or someone else's pending review) and before
233	  all of S3's other checks. So an applied suggestion gets this message even when the PR is closed,
234	  the head moved, the line is outdated or the user can't push.
235	- [ ] AC3: Given an instance upgraded from a version without this feature, when existing review
236	  comments are shown, then they render as before, none is marked applied, and their suggestions
237	  can still be applied. A migration test checks that existing comment rows get the zero values.
238	- [ ] AC4: Given the applying commit no longer exists in the base repository (force-pushed away
239	  and garbage-collected), when the comment is shown, then the marker still shows "Applied by" and
240	  the short SHA, unlinked. While the commit still exists, even after a force-push, it stays
241	  linked. For a fork PR, the link points at the base repository, which holds the PR's commits
242	  under `refs/pull/<index>/head`.
243	- [ ] AC5: Given the comment is deleted after being applied, when the PR is viewed, then the commit
244	  stays on the branch and the Conversation and Files tabs render with no error. The timeline's
245	  "added 1 commit" entry is unchanged. Nothing else refers to the deleted comment.
246	- [ ] AC6: Given a suggestion is applied, then its conversation stays as it was: an unresolved
247	  conversation is not resolved. *Pending customer question 3 on #151; see Open Questions.*
248	- [ ] AC7: Given the commit is pushed but saving the applied state fails, then Apply still reports
249	  success, because the commit is on the branch, and the error is logged. After the reload, the
250	  comment shows as Outdated without a marker. Applying it again is refused as outdated (S3 AC3)
251	  and commits nothing.
252	- [ ] AC8: Given the applier's account is deleted later, when the comment is shown, then the
253	  marker reads "Applied by Ghost" with the SHA still shown, and nothing errors. This is Gitea's
254	  usual display for a deleted user.
255	- [ ] AC9: Given the reviewer edits the comment after it was applied, even changing the
256	  suggestion, when it is shown, then the marker stays and there is no Apply button. To suggest
257	  something new, the reviewer posts a new comment.
258	- [ ] AC10: Given two people apply the same suggestion at the same time, then exactly one commit
259	  is made and the comment records that one commit. The other person gets S3's "This branch has new
260	  commits since the page was loaded" (S3 AC4).
261
262	### Out of Scope
263
264	- A timeline entry of its own ("ben applied a suggestion from ana"). The push already adds
265	  Gitea's "added 1 commit" entry with the suggestion's commit message (see Design Decision).
266	- Resolving the conversation on apply, unless the customer answers yes to question 3 (AC6).
267	- Undoing an applied suggestion: revert it like any other commit. The marker stays.
268	- Showing the applied state in the API (S7).
269	- Several applied suggestions per comment (S6). S3 only applies a comment with exactly one block.
270
271	### Open Questions
272
273	- **Customer question 3 (resolve on apply)**, for AC6: still unanswered on #151. The default is
274	  to not resolve, as S3 did for its open questions. If the customer says yes, resolving becomes
275	  a small follow-up: one `MarkConversation` call after the applied state is saved.
276
277	### Design Decision
278
279	**Decision:** Add three columns to `comment`, all `NOT NULL` with a default, so existing rows get
280	zero values in the same `ALTER TABLE` (`docs/models-migrations.md`):
281	- `suggestion_applied_by_id` (`BIGINT DEFAULT 0`)
282	- `suggestion_applied_commit` (`VARCHAR(64) DEFAULT ''`)
283	- `suggestion_applied_unix` (`BIGINT DEFAULT 0`)
284
285	The migration is the next free id in `models/migrations/v1_27`.
286
287	S3's `ApplySuggestion` (`services/repository/files/suggestion.go`) changes in two places:
288	- **Before committing:** after its 404 checks, it returns a new `ErrSuggestionAlreadyApplied` when
289	  the column is set (AC2).
290	- **After committing:** it takes the new commit's SHA from `ChangeRepoFiles`' response, which S3
291	  currently discards, and calls a new `issues_model.MarkSuggestionApplied(ctx, comment, doer, sha)`.
292	  That is one `UPDATE comment SET ... WHERE id = ? AND suggestion_applied_commit = ''`, so a
293	  comment is never marked twice (AC10).
294
295	Git isn't part of the database transaction, so the commit comes first. A failed save is logged
296	and doesn't fail the request (AC7).
297
298	The two comment templates already set S3's `data-suggestion-apply-*` attributes:
299	- They skip those attributes when the comment is applied.
300	- They add `data-suggestion-applied-*` attributes instead: the applier's name, the short SHA, and
301	  the commit link only if the commit exists in the base repository (AC4).
302	- `suggestion.ts` draws the marker in the suggestion header, where S3 puts Apply.
303
304	**Alternatives Considered:**
305	- *A separate `review_suggestion` table, one row per suggestion.* It's cleaner once S6 allows
306	  several per comment. But S3 applies only comments with exactly one block, so for now it's a join
307	  for nothing.
308	- *Store nothing; detect "applied" by comparing the current file to the suggestion.* No migration,
309	  but it's wrong when the same text arrives another way, and it can't say who applied it.
310	- *A new timeline comment type, "ben applied a suggestion from ana".* This was this spec's first
311	  version. It needs:
312	  - a new `CommentType`, template branch and API type string;
313	  - a reference to the code comment, which breaks when that comment is deleted. With
314	    `RefCommentID`, the API's `ToTimelineComment` returns nil when the comment is gone;
315	  - care not to expose a comment from the applier's own pending review.
316
317	  The push already adds "added 1 commit" with the default message "Apply suggestion from @ana on
318	  main.go", and the marker sits on the comment itself. So the entry repeats information at real
319	  cost.
320	- *Nullable columns (this spec's first version).* `docs/models-migrations.md` says old rows would
321	  hold NULL, which `WHERE col = 0` or `= ''` doesn't match. `NOT NULL DEFAULT` gives old rows the
322	  same zero values as new ones (AC3).
323
324	**Rationale:** The columns sit next to the data they describe. Checking for "applied" adds no join
325	or lookup to the Apply path. S3's existing data-attribute and `suggestion.ts` path draws the marker
326	the same way in both tabs.
327
328	**Consequences:**
329	- A schema migration with a migration test.
330	- If S6 allows several applied suggestions per comment, these columns move to their own table.
331	- Rendering an applied comment costs one commit-existence check against the base repository
332	  (AC4).
333	- An applied comment also shows as Outdated, because its line changed (S3 marks it). The marker
334	  says why.
335	- S3's two templates gain a second set of attributes. A shared subtemplate for both sets would
336	  stop them drifting; that was optional item 7 in the #179 review.
337
338	### Scope
339
340	medium
341
342	### Scope Justification
343
344	- **Model:** three `comment` columns, `MarkSuggestionApplied`, and a migration with a migration
345	  test (AC3).
346	- **Service:** S3's `ApplySuggestion` gains the already-applied check, records the commit after
347	  it's pushed, and a new error case in the web handler (AC2, AC7, AC10).
348	- **Templates and frontend:** two comment templates gain the applied attributes, and
349	  `suggestion.ts` draws the marker, with Vitest tests (AC1, AC4, AC8, AC9).
350	- **Tests:** an integration test that applies a suggestion and checks the marker, the re-apply
351	  refusal and a deleted comment, sharing one PR setup like S3's (AC1, AC2, AC5).
352	- **Not included:** no new comment type and no API change.

357	=========== #158
358	S5. Suggest a change across several lines open ['enhancement', 'scope: medium']
359	Closes #158
360
361	## What changed
362
363	A reviewer can now comment on a range of new-side lines in Files changed. Click a line number, shift-click another in the same hunk, then click `+` on the last line of the range. The comment form and the posted thread are headed "Lines 18–22". "Suggest change" pre-fills every line of the range, and a suggestion renders with all the range's lines removed.
364
365	- **Storage:** the range start is `StartLine` in the comment's existing `CommentMetaData` JSON field. `Line` stays the range end, so thread placement, replies, the API and old rows are unchanged. No migration. `Comment.RangeStartLine()` and `Comment.RangeOriginalLines()` are the helpers S3/S6/S7 can use.
366	- **Server (`services/pull/review.go`):**
367	  - `CreateCodeComment` takes a `startLine`.
368	  - It checks that the range is on the new side and ends after it starts before it creates a pending review, so a refused range doesn't leave an empty review behind.
369	  - For a range it stores the hunk up to the range end and refuses (`ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid` → 400) a range that isn't in one hunk.
370	  - A reply inherits its thread's range.
371	- **Invalidation:** a range comment goes Outdated when the text of any line in its range changed at the new head (`checkRangeInvalidation`). The head commit is looked up once per push, and each file is read once, however many range comments it has. Single-line comments keep the existing blame check.
372	- **Frontend:**
373	  - `repo-diff-range.ts` handles click / shift-click on new-side line numbers, or Enter / Shift+Enter from the keyboard (PR diffs give those cells `tabindex="0"`). It refuses selections across hunks, expanded context or sides, with a toast.
374	  - The comment-form submit in `repo-diff.ts` now shows the server's error message when the POST fails, instead of failing silently. This can happen when a range was picked in a whitespace-ignored or single-commit view whose hunks differ from the full PR diff.
375	  - The `+` handler fetches the form with `start_line`/`line`, and the template renders the header.
376	  - S2's `initSuggestChangeButton` takes the range's lines.
377	  - S1's renderer splits the original on `\n`.
378
379	## Why
380
381	Reviewers could only suggest single-line changes. This covers #158 AC1–AC15. Apply-a-range was moved out of scope to S3 #156 / S6 #159 (see the spec discussion on the issue).

// ApplySuggestion commits a review comment's suggestion to the pull request's head branch (#156)
func ApplySuggestion(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.ApplySuggestionForm)
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		ctx.NotFound(nil)
		return
	}
	if ctx.HasError() {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.GetErrMsg())
		return
	}
	comment, err := issues_model.GetCommentByID(ctx, ctx.PathParamInt64("id"))
	if issues_model.IsErrCommentNotExist(err) {
		ctx.NotFound(err)
		return
	} else if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetCommentByID", err)
		return
	}
	if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadPullRequest", err)
		return
	}

	err = files_service.ApplySuggestion(ctx, ctx.Doer, issue.PullRequest, comment, form.HeadCommitID, form.Message)
	if err != nil {
		applySuggestionError(ctx, issue.PullRequest.HeadBranch, err)
		return
	}
	ctx.JSONOK() // the page reloads to show the new commit
}

// applySuggestionError answers a refused Apply. Messages are plain text (TrString), since the page shows them
// with textContent: hook output must never become HTML.
func applySuggestionError(ctx *context.Context, headBranch string, err error) {
	var errProtected files_service.ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch
	var errPushRejected *git.ErrPushRejected
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionNotApplicable):
		ctx.NotFound(err)
	case errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionPermission):
		ctx.HTTPError(http.StatusForbidden) // AC2
	case errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionPullClosed):
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.diff.suggestion.pull_closed")) // AC5
	case errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionHeadMoved), git.IsErrPushOutOfDate(err):
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.diff.suggestion.head_moved")) // AC4
	case errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionOutdated):
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.diff.suggestion.outdated")) // AC3
	case errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionNoChange):
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.diff.suggestion.no_change")) // AC10
	case errors.As(err, &errProtected):
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.cannot_commit_to_protected_branch", errProtected.Branch)) // AC6, the web editor's message
	case files_service.IsErrUserCannotCommit(err), pull_service.IsErrFilePathProtected(err):
		// what the AC6 pre-check doesn't cover: required signed commits and protected file patterns
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.cannot_commit_to_protected_branch", headBranch))
	case errors.As(err, &errPushRejected):
		if errPushRejected.Message == "" {
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.push_rejected_no_message"))
		} else {
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.push_rejected") + "\n" + errPushRejected.Message) // a pre-receive hook
		}
	default:
		ctx.ServerError("ApplySuggestion", err)
	}
}

======
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package files

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	git_model "gitea.dev/models/git"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	access_model "gitea.dev/models/perm/access"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	"gitea.dev/modules/gitrepo"
)

var (
	// ErrSuggestionNotApplicable means the comment has no suggestion that can be applied: not a new-side code comment
	// on this pull request, or not exactly one suggestion block (#156 AC7)
	ErrSuggestionNotApplicable = errors.New("the comment has no suggestion to apply")
	// ErrSuggestionPullClosed means the pull request is closed or merged, or has no head branch to commit to (#156 AC5)
	ErrSuggestionPullClosed = errors.New("the pull request is closed or its head branch is gone")
	// ErrSuggestionPermission means the doer cannot push to the head branch (#156 AC2)
	ErrSuggestionPermission = errors.New("the doer cannot push to the head branch")
	// ErrSuggestionHeadMoved means the head branch has new commits since the page was loaded (#156 AC4)
	ErrSuggestionHeadMoved = errors.New("the head branch has moved")
	// ErrSuggestionOutdated means the commented line no longer reads as it did when the suggestion was written (#156 AC3)
	ErrSuggestionOutdated = errors.New("the suggestion is outdated")
	// ErrSuggestionNoChange means applying the suggestion would leave the file as it is (#156 AC10)
	ErrSuggestionNoChange = errors.New("the suggestion makes no changes")
)

// ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch means branch protection stops the doer from pushing to the head branch (#156 AC6)
type ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch struct {
	Branch string
}

func (err ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("branch %q is protected", err.Branch)
}

// CanApplySuggestions checks what does not depend on the comment: the pull request is open, has a head branch
// (AGit pull requests have none) and the doer can push to it. It returns the head branch's commit ID.
func CanApplySuggestions(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest) (string, error) {
	if doer == nil {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPermission
	}
	if err := pr.LoadIssue(ctx); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if pr.HasMerged || pr.Issue.IsClosed || pr.Flow != issues_model.PullRequestFlowGithub {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed
	}
	if err := pr.LoadHeadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if pr.HeadRepo == nil {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed // the fork was deleted
	}
	if pr.HeadRepo.IsArchived {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPermission // nobody may push to an archived fork; the route only checks the base repo
	}
	headPerm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pr.HeadRepo, doer)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	// includes "Allow edits from maintainers" on fork pull requests
	if !issues_model.CanMaintainerWriteToBranch(ctx, headPerm, pr.HeadBranch, doer) {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPermission
	}
	headGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.HeadRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer closer.Close()
	headCommitID, err := headGitRepo.GetBranchCommitID(pr.HeadBranch)
	if git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed // the head branch was deleted
	}
	return headCommitID, err
}

// ApplySuggestion commits the comment's single suggestion to the pull request's head branch, replacing the
// commented line. expectedHeadSHA is the head commit the page showed; message may be empty for the default.
func ApplySuggestion(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, comment *issues_model.Comment, expectedHeadSHA, message string) error {
	original := comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()
	if comment.IssueID != pr.IssueID || !original.Has() {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}
	blocks := comment.SuggestionBlocks(ctx)
	if len(blocks) != 1 {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}
	// a pending review's comments are visible only to its reviewer (FetchCodeComments, the API), so for anyone
	// else the suggestion doesn't exist; applying it would publish a draft into the branch history
	if err := comment.LoadReview(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if comment.Review != nil && comment.Review.Type == issues_model.ReviewTypePending && (doer == nil || comment.Review.ReviewerID != doer.ID) {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}

	headCommitID, err := CanApplySuggestions(ctx, doer, pr)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if headCommitID != expectedHeadSHA {
		return ErrSuggestionHeadMoved
	}

	// the web editor's check, so the user gets our message rather than the pre-receive hook's output
	protectedBranch, err := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(ctx, pr.HeadRepo.ID, pr.HeadBranch)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if protectedBranch != nil {
		protectedBranch.Repo = pr.HeadRepo
		canPush := protectedBranch.CanUserPush(ctx, doer)
		if !canPush && protectedBranch.UnprotectedFilePatterns != "" {
			canPush = protectedBranch.IsUnprotectedFile(protectedBranch.GetUnprotectedFilePatterns(), comment.TreePath)
		}
		if !canPush {
			return ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch{Branch: pr.HeadBranch}
		}
	}

	if comment.Invalidated {
		return ErrSuggestionOutdated // the page hides Apply on outdated comments, but a page loaded earlier may still post
	}

	headGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.HeadRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer closer.Close()
	headCommit, err := headGitRepo.GetCommit(headCommitID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	blob, err := headCommit.GetBlobByPath(comment.TreePath)

}

**The spec review asks #159 to settle its open question on batch size. What should the maximum number of suggestions in one batch be? Whatever you pick becomes an AC: the client refuses to add another, and a direct POST over the limit returns 400 with nothing committed.**

Options:
- **50 (Recommended)** - Keeps the number already proposed in the issue, so the review only needs it turned into an AC.
- **20** - A smaller cap. Each batch reads and edits fewer files in a single commit.
- **No limit** - Drop the cap entirely and say why in the spec. The 'batch over the maximum' case then becomes 'not applicable'.

**S5 (#158) adds multi-line range comments, and its PR says 'Apply-a-range was moved out of scope to S3 #156 / S6 #159'. S3 merged with single-line apply only. Should S6 also apply range suggestions, or only the single-line suggestions S3 can apply, using S5's ranges just for the overlap check?**

Options:
- **Single-line only (Recommended)** - S6 batches what S3 can apply. Range suggestions get no 'Add to batch' button, and applying ranges becomes a follow-up issue. Two single-line comments overlap only when they're on the same line. Keeps the issue medium.
- **Include ranges** - S6 also applies range suggestions and uses S5's start..end ranges for overlap. S6 then depends on S5 merging first, adds range-apply logic and tests, and is closer to large.


**Answer:** 50 (Recommended), Could we include ranges but split it into a medium and small?". Read the answers carefully — they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed — and follow what they actually say.

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, the team
references logs in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page,
D5; later sprint pages also accept the PR, and the issue comment satisfies both).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log. The
PR's Test Evidence section has its own **AI-written tests** line, which names the tests AI wrote or
changed and how you checked their expected values (`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, "Pull request format").

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
=====
# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint<N>/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- These are **not** logs and get no full credit: a summary of a session, paraphrased prompts, a
  share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it (Sprint 3 page).
- Attachments (screenshots, snippets) go in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`.
- Log **every** session, including ones that went nowhere. Grading is on how complete the record
  is, not on whether AI helped.

## Where logs are referenced

- **Issue comments only.** Each contributor posts their own `### AI Assistance — @username` comment
  on the issue, with full `https://github.com/...` links to their logs. Format:
  [`.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md`](../.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md).
- **Not** in PR descriptions or PR comments. The PR has a short AI-use note with no log link. The
  AI Log Instructions page says "Issue/PR comments" and the Sprint 3 page "the issue or PR", but
  the Sprint 1 page narrows it to issue comments only; the team keeps that rule, which satisfies
  all three.
- Each teammate posts their own comment, including reviewers who used AI to review.
- No AI used? Post an issue comment saying so, and keep your folder with its `.gitkeep`.
- The sprint report lists each member's tools, session count, folder link, and 2–3 sentences on
  lessons learned.

**Title:** S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines

**Labels:** `enhancement`, `scope: small` · **Assignee:** Jack-Donohue · **Milestone:** Sprint 3 · **Parent:** #151

---

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #156 (S3, merged in #179) and #158 (S5)

As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion on a range of lines with one click, so
that multi-line feedback lands on my branch the same way single-line feedback does.

### User Scenario

Ana selects lines 18–22 of `main.go` and suggests replacing them with two lines (S5). Ben clicks
**Apply suggestion**, keeps the default message "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go" and
confirms. The page reloads, and the PR has one more commit in which lines 18–22 are replaced by
Ana's two lines and nothing else in the file changed.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned as in S3 (#156): HTTP 400 with the message shown on the
page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on lines L–M (S5) and a user who can push to the head branch, when
  they apply it, then exactly one commit is added that replaces lines L–M with the block's lines
  in order, matching S5 AC5's diff. No line before L or after M changes. The commit message
  follows S3 AC1 (default "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>", editable).
- [ ] AC2: Given the block is empty or holds one blank line, when it is applied, then the commit
  deletes lines L–M, or replaces them with one blank line (S5 AC6, S3 AC12).
- [ ] AC3: Given any line in L–M (first, middle or last) differs at head from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or the file now has fewer than M lines, or it was deleted or
  renamed, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see "This suggestion is
  outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given a range suggestion, then the Apply button is shown or hidden under the same
  conditions as a single-line one (S3 AC2, AC5, AC7, AC9), and a direct POST gets S3's responses:
  403 for a user who can't push, 400 "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request
  whose branch still exists." for a closed or merged PR, 400 "This branch has new commits since
  the page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." for a stale head, and `Cannot commit to
  protected branch "<branch>".` for a protected branch.
- [ ] AC5: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, including a range that ends
  on the last line, when a range suggestion is applied, then the new lines use the file's line
  ending and the file's final-newline state is unchanged (S3 AC11).
- [ ] AC6: Given a range suggestion whose block equals lines L–M, when applied, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code." (S3 AC10).
- [ ] AC7: Given a single-line suggestion, then applying it behaves exactly as before: S3's
  existing tests pass without changes.

### Out of Scope

- Applying several suggestions in one commit (S6, #159), which reuses this.
- Recording "applied" (S4, #157) and the API (S7, #160).
- Re-anchoring a range whose lines moved but didn't change: it is refused as outdated, like S3.

### Open Questions

- None.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's `applySuggestionToContent` in
`services/repository/files/suggestion.go` to replace lines start..end instead of one line, where
a single-line comment is the range [Line, Line], and check every line of the range against S5's
`Comment.RangeOriginalLines()` before replacing.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A separate `applyRangeSuggestionToContent`.* Leaves S3's function untouched, but duplicates its
  CRLF, final-newline and outdated handling, so the two would drift apart.
- *Build a patch from S5's rendered diff and run `git apply` in a temp clone.* S3 already rejected
  this: fuzzy matching can land the change on the wrong lines, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` does.

**Rationale:** One function keeps a single place for line-ending handling, and S3's tests become
the regression check for the one-line case (AC7).

**Consequences:** `applySuggestionToContent` gets a start line. S6 (#159) calls it per suggestion,
bottom-up, so a batch can hold ranges. A range that moved but didn't change is refused.

### Scope

small

### Scope Justification

One service function in `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` (range replace plus a range
outdated check) and S3's Apply attribute offered on range comments, with unit tests for AC1–AC3,
AC5 and AC6 and one integration case for AC4. No new route, UI or schema change.

---

# #159 spec revision (S6)

review. Replace `#S6A` with the new small issue's number before posting (it appears in both parts).

- The batch limit is 50.

---

## Part 1: issue body

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #156 (S3, merged in #179), #157 (S4), #158 (S5) and #S6A (S6a)

As a PR author, I want to pick several suggestions and apply them together so that my branch gets
one commit instead of one per suggestion.

### User Scenario

Ana leaves four suggestions on two files. Ben clicks **Add to batch** on three of them; a bar at the
bottom shows "3 suggestions selected · Apply". He applies them and the PR gets one commit changing
both files, and all three comments are marked applied.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the batch Apply POST are returned as in S3 (#156): HTTP 400 with the message shown on
the page, unless an AC says otherwise. "Nothing is committed" means the head branch is unchanged
and no suggestion is marked applied.

- [ ] AC1: Given several selected suggestions, when applied, then one commit containing all of
  them is added and each is marked applied (S4) with that commit. The form is prefilled with
  "Apply <N> suggestions from code review" and can be edited, as in S3 AC1. Each reviewer other
  than the applier is credited as in S3 (customer question 1 default).
- [ ] AC2: Given two suggestions on the same file whose line ranges share a line (a single-line
  suggestion's range is its one line; a range suggestion's is S5's start–end), when the user tries
  to add the second to the batch, then it is refused with "overlaps another suggestion in this
  batch". A direct POST with both gets 400 with the same message and nothing is committed.
- [ ] AC3: Given one suggestion in the batch is outdated (S3 AC3, S6a AC3), when applied, then
  nothing is committed and the message is S3's "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed
  since it was written." followed by that suggestion's file and line (all or nothing).
- [ ] AC4: Given suggestions were added to the batch but not applied, when the page is reloaded,
  then no batch bar is shown and every suggestion shows **Add to batch** again (the batch is not
  stored server-side). Checked by an E2E test, since there is no server state to assert.
- [ ] AC5: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch, then no suggestion shows **Add to
  batch**, and a direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing. A signed-out viewer sees no button,
  and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing (S3 AC2).
- [ ] AC6: Given the PR is closed or merged, its head branch was deleted, or it uses AGit flow,
  then no **Add to batch** button is shown, and a direct POST returns 400 with "Suggestions can
  only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists." and commits nothing (S3
  AC5).
- [ ] AC7: Given the head branch moved since the page loaded, when the batch is applied with the
  old head SHA, then nothing is committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the
  page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." (S3 AC4).
- [ ] AC8: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when the batch is applied,
  then nothing is committed and they see `Cannot commit to protected branch "<branch>".` (S3 AC6).
- [ ] AC9: Given two suggestions in one file that change line counts differently (one replaces
  one line with three, one further down deletes its line), when applied together, then the
  committed file is the same as applying them one at a time, and no other line changes.
- [ ] AC10: Given an already-applied suggestion (S4), then it has no **Add to batch** button
  (S4 AC1), and a direct POST that includes it returns 400 with "This suggestion has already been
  applied." (S4 AC2) followed by its file and line, and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC11: Given a batch of one suggestion, when applied, then the commit's content and default
  message are the same as S3's **Apply suggestion** on that suggestion.
- [ ] AC12: Given an empty batch, then the batch bar is hidden. A direct POST with no suggestions
  returns 400 and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC13: Given a suggestion already in the batch, then its button reads **Remove from batch**,
  so it can't be added twice. A direct POST that lists the same suggestion twice returns 400 and
  commits nothing.
- [ ] AC14: Given a batch of 50 suggestions, when the user tries to add another, then it is
  refused with "A batch can hold at most 50 suggestions." A direct POST with 51 returns 400 with
  the same message and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC15: Given a range suggestion (S5) and a single-line suggestion in the same file that don't
  overlap, when both are applied in one batch, then the commit applies each exactly as S6a AC1 and
  S3 AC1 would on their own.

### Out of Scope

- Batches across PRs; saving a batch for later.
- Applying a single range suggestion on its own (S6a, #S6A).

### Open Questions

- ~~Is there a maximum batch size?~~ Resolved: 50 (AC14).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's service to take a list of comment IDs and build one
`ChangeRepoFiles` call with one entry per file, applying edits in a file bottom-up so earlier
replacements don't shift later line numbers.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply each suggestion as its own commit in a loop.* Easy, but not atomic: a failure halfway
  leaves a partial result, and it is not what the user asked for.
- *Store pending batches server-side.* Survives reloads, but needs a table and cleanup for
  something the user does in one sitting.

**Rationale:** One `ChangeRepoFiles` call is a single atomic commit, and bottom-up edits are a
simple, testable way to avoid line drift.

**Consequences:** S3's function signature changes; S7's batch endpoint reuses it.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

- **Service:** `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` takes a list of comments and runs S3's
  checks on each (S4's already-applied check, overlap, the limit), then applies S6a's range-aware
  edit per file bottom-up in one `ChangeRepoFiles` (AC1–AC3, AC9–AC15).
- **Web:** one route in `routers/web/web.go`, a handler in `routers/web/repo/pull_review.go`
  reusing S3's error mapping, and a form in `services/forms` (AC5–AC8).
- **Frontend:** **Add to batch** / **Remove from batch** and the batch bar in
  `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`, with Vitest tests (AC2, AC12–AC14), plus a few locale strings.
- **Tests:** unit tests for line drift and overlap, integration tests for AC5–AC8 and AC10 sharing
  one PR setup, and one E2E test for AC4.
- No schema change. Medium fits: one service change, one UI bar, one commit.

---

  batch". A direct POST with both gets 400 with the same message and nothing is committed.
- [ ] AC3: Given one suggestion in the batch is outdated (S3 AC3, S6a AC3), when applied, then
  nothing is committed and the message is S3's "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed
  since it was written." followed by that suggestion's file and line (all or nothing).
- [ ] AC4: Given suggestions were added to the batch but not applied, when the page is reloaded,
  then no batch bar is shown and every suggestion shows **Add to batch** again (the batch is not
  stored server-side). Checked by an E2E test, since there is no server state to assert.
- [ ] AC5: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch, then no suggestion shows **Add to
  batch**, and a direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing. A signed-out viewer sees no button,
  and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing (S3 AC2).
- [ ] AC6: Given the PR is closed or merged, its head branch was deleted, or it uses AGit flow,
  then no **Add to batch** button is shown, and a direct POST returns 400 with "Suggestions can
  only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists." and commits nothing (S3
  AC5).
- [ ] AC7: Given the head branch moved since the page loaded, when the batch is applied with the
  old head SHA, then nothing is committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the
  page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." (S3 AC4).
- [ ] AC8: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when the batch is applied,
  then nothing is committed and they see `Cannot commit to protected branch "<branch>".` (S3 AC6).
- [ ] AC9: Given two suggestions in one file that change line counts differently (one replaces
  one line with three, one further down deletes its line), when applied together, then the
  committed file is the same as applying them one at a time, and no other line changes.
- [ ] AC10: Given an already-applied suggestion (S4), then it has no **Add to batch** button
  (S4 AC1), and a direct POST that includes it returns 400 with "This suggestion has already been
  applied." (S4 AC2) followed by its file and line, and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC11: Given a batch of one suggestion, when applied, then the commit's content and default
  message are the same as S3's **Apply suggestion** on that suggestion.
- [ ] AC12: Given an empty batch, then the batch bar is hidden. A direct POST with no suggestions
  returns 400 and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC13: Given a suggestion already in the batch, then its button reads **Remove from batch**,
  so it can't be added twice. A direct POST that lists the same suggestion twice returns 400 and
  commits nothing.
- [ ] AC14: Given a batch of 50 suggestions, when the user tries to add another, then it is
  refused with "A batch can hold at most 50 suggestions." A direct POST with 51 returns 400 with
  the same message and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC15: Given a range suggestion (S5) and a single-line suggestion in the same file that don't
  overlap, when both are applied in one batch, then the commit applies each exactly as S6a AC1 and
  S3 AC1 would on their own.

### Out of Scope

- Batches across PRs; saving a batch for later.
- Applying a single range suggestion on its own (S6a, #S6A).

### Open Questions

- ~~Is there a maximum batch size?~~ Resolved: 50 (AC14).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's service to take a list of comment IDs and build one
`ChangeRepoFiles` call with one entry per file, applying edits in a file bottom-up so earlier
replacements don't shift later line numbers.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply each suggestion as its own commit in a loop.* Easy, but not atomic: a failure halfway
  leaves a partial result, and it is not what the user asked for.
- *Store pending batches server-side.* Survives reloads, but needs a table and cleanup for
  something the user does in one sitting.

**Rationale:** One `ChangeRepoFiles` call is a single atomic commit, and bottom-up edits are a
simple, testable way to avoid line drift.

**Consequences:** S3's function signature changes; S7's batch endpoint reuses it.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

- **Service:** `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` takes a list of comments and runs S3's
  checks on each (S4's already-applied check, overlap, the limit), then applies S6a's range-aware
  edit per file bottom-up in one `ChangeRepoFiles` (AC1–AC3, AC9–AC15).
- **Web:** one route in `routers/web/web.go`, a handler in `routers/web/repo/pull_review.go`
  reusing S3's error mapping, and a form in `services/forms` (AC5–AC8).
- **Frontend:** **Add to batch** / **Remove from batch** and the batch bar in
  `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`, with Vitest tests (AC2, AC12–AC14), plus a few locale strings.
- **Tests:** unit tests for line drift and overlap, integration tests for AC5–AC8 and AC10 sharing
  one PR setup, and one E2E test for AC4.
- No schema change. Medium fits: one service change, one UI bar, one commit.

=========== #189
S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines open ['enhancement', 'scope: small'] Jack-Donohue None
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #156 (S3, merged in #179) and #158 (S5)

As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion on a range of lines with one click, so
that multi-line feedback lands on my branch the same way single-line feedback does.

### User Scenario

Ana selects lines 18–22 of `main.go` and suggests replacing them with two lines (S5). Ben clicks
**Apply suggestion**, keeps the default message "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go" and
confirms. The page reloads, and the PR has one more commit in which lines 18–22 are replaced by
Ana's two lines and nothing else in the file changed.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned as in S3 (#156): HTTP 400 with the message shown on the
page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on lines L–M (S5) and a user who can push to the head branch, when
  they apply it, then exactly one commit is added that replaces lines L–M with the block's lines
  in order, matching S5 AC5's diff. No line before L or after M changes. The commit message
  follows S3 AC1 (default "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>", editable).
- [ ] AC2: Given the block is empty or holds one blank line, when it is applied, then the commit
  deletes lines L–M, or replaces them with one blank line (S5 AC6, S3 AC12).
- [ ] AC3: Given any line in L–M (first, middle or last) differs at head from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or the file now has fewer than M lines, or it was deleted or
  renamed, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see "This suggestion is
  outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given a range suggestion, then the Apply button is shown or hidden under the same
  conditions as a single-line one (S3 AC2, AC5, AC7, AC9), and a direct POST gets S3's responses:
  403 for a user who can't push, 400 "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request
  whose branch still exists." for a closed or merged PR, 400 "This branch has new commits since
  the page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." for a stale head, and `Cannot commit to
  protected branch "<branch>".` for a protected branch.
- [ ] AC5: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, including a range that ends
  on the last line, when a range suggestion is applied, then the new lines use the file's line
  ending and the file's final-newline state is unchanged (S3 AC11).
- [ ] AC6: Given a range suggestion whose block equals lines L–M, when applied, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code." (S3 AC10).
- [ ] AC7: Given a single-line suggestion, then applying it behaves exactly as before: S3's
  existing tests pass without changes.

### Out of Scope

- Applying several suggestions in one commit (S6, #159), which reuses this.
- Recording "applied" (S4, #157) and the API (S7, #160).
- Re-anchoring a range whose lines moved but didn't change: it is refused as outdated, like S3.

### Open Questions

- None.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's `applySuggestionToContent` in
`services/repository/files/suggestion.go` to replace lines start..end instead of one line, where
a single-line comment is the range [Line, Line], and check every line of the range against S5's
`Comment.RangeOriginalLines()` before replacing.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A separate `applyRangeSuggestionToContent`.* Leaves S3's function untouched, but duplicates its
  CRLF, final-newline and outdated handling, so the two would drift apart.
- *Build a patch from S5's rendered diff and run `git apply` in a temp clone.* S3 already rejected
  this: fuzzy matching can land the change on the wrong lines, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` does.

**Rationale:** One function keeps a single place for line-ending handling, and S3's tests become
the regression check for the one-line case (AC7).

**Consequences:** `applySuggestionToContent` gets a start line. S6 (#159) calls it per suggestion,
bottom-up, so a batch can hold ranges. A range that moved but didn't change is refused.

### Scope

small

### Scope Justification

One service function in `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` (range replace plus a range
outdated check) and S3's Apply attribute offered on range comments, with unit tests for AC1–AC3,
AC5 and AC6 and one integration case for AC4. No new route, UI or schema change.

		innerEnding := ending

			innerEnding = "\n"

		}
		newLines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(suggestion, "\n"), "\n")
		replacement = strings.Join(newLines, innerEnding) + ending
	}

	before := strings.Join(lines[:idx], "")
	if replacement == "" && ending == "" && idx > 0 {
		// deleting a last line that has no newline: the line before it becomes last and loses its newline,
		// so the file still ends without one (#156 AC11)
		prev := lines[idx-1]
		before = strings.Join(lines[:idx-1], "") + strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(prev, "\n"), "\r")
	}
	result := before + replacement + strings.Join(lines[idx+1:], "")
	if result == content {
		return "", ErrSuggestionNoChange
	}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/markup/markdown"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

// SuggestionContextLines returns the new-side lines the stored patch shows above the commented line, in file
// order. Applying a suggestion checks them too, since blame-based invalidation can miss the commented line
// moving onto an identical one, like another "}" (#156 AC3).
func (c *Comment) SuggestionContextLines() []string {
	if !c.SuggestionOriginalLine().Has() {
		return nil
	}
	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n"), "\n")
	hunkStart := -1
	for i, line := range lines {
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "@@") {
			hunkStart = i
		}
	}
	if hunkStart < 0 {
		return nil
	}
	var above []string
	for _, line := range lines[hunkStart+1 : len(lines)-1] { // the last line is the commented one
		if line != "" && (line[0] == ' ' || line[0] == '+') {
			above = append(above, line[1:])
		} // "-" is the old side, "\" is "No newline at end of file"
	}
	return above
}

// SuggestionBlocks returns the text of each ```suggestion block in the comment, found the way the
// rendered page finds them (#154 AC9). An empty block is "", one blank line is "\n".
func (c *Comment) SuggestionBlocks(ctx context.Context) []string {
	return markdown.FencedCodeBlocks(ctx, []byte(c.Content), "suggestion")
}

// SuggestionCommitMessage is the default message for committing the comment's suggestion (#156 AC1).
// The poster must be loaded.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionCommitMessage() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("Apply suggestion from @%s on %s", c.Poster.Name, c.TreePath)
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// For a multi-line comment it returns every line of the range, joined by "\n".
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 {
		lines, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
		if !ok {
			return optional.None[string]()
		}
		return optional.Some(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

// RangeOriginalLines returns lines RangeStartLine..Line of a multi-line code comment as the
// reviewer saw them, false if the stored patch doesn't hold all of them.
func (c *Comment) RangeOriginalLines() ([]string, bool) {
	start := c.RangeStartLine()
	if start <= 0 || c.Line < start {
		return nil, false
	}
	return PatchLastNewLines(c.Patch, int(c.Line-start+1))
}

// PatchLastNewLines returns the last n new-side lines of a one-hunk patch, which end at the
// commented line, skipping removed lines. False if the hunk has fewer than n.
func PatchLastNewLines(patch string, n int) ([]string, bool) {
	rows := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(patch, "\n"), "\n")
	lines := make([]string, n)
	for i := len(rows) - 1; i >= 0 && n > 0; i-- {
		switch {
		case rows[i] == "" || rows[i][0] == '@':
			return nil, false // reached the hunk header
		case rows[i][0] == '+' || rows[i][0] == ' ':
			n--
			lines[n] = rows[i][1:]
		}
	}
	return lines, n == 0
}
func (c *Comment) DiffSide() string {
	if c.Line < 0 {
		return "previous"
	}
	return "proposed"
}

// UnsignedLine returns the LOC of the code comment without + or -
func (c *Comment) UnsignedLine() uint64 {
	if c.Line < 0 {
		return uint64(c.Line * -1)
	}
	return uint64(c.Line)
}

// RangeStartLine returns the first line of a multi-line code comment, or 0 for a single-line one
func (c *Comment) RangeStartLine() int64 {
	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return c.CommentMetaData.StartLine
}

// CodeCommentLink returns the url to a comment in code
func (c *Comment) CodeCommentLink(ctx context.Context) string {
	err := c.LoadIssue(ctx)
	if err != nil { // Silently dropping errors :unamused:
		log.Error("LoadIssue(%d): %v", c.IssueID, err)
		return ""
	}
	err = c.Issue.LoadRepo(ctx)
	if err != nil { // Silently dropping errors :unamused:
		log.Error("loadRepo(%d): %v", c.Issue.RepoID, err)
		return ""
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s/files#%s", c.Issue.Link(), c.HashTag())
}

// MetaCloseReason returns the reason recorded on a close comment; comments without metadata have none.
// The duplicate target is not included: load it with LoadCloseDuplicateIssue.
func (c *Comment) MetaCloseReason() CloseReasonOptions {
	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {
		return CloseReasonOptions{}
	}
	return CloseReasonOptions{Reason: c.CommentMetaData.CloseReason, Text: c.CommentMetaData.CloseReasonText}
}

## Context

Both specs are posted. The #159 spec revision answers @controlled-opposition's review; #189 is new.
Current state (checked 2026-11-17 against `origin`):
- **S3 (#156)** is merged (#179): `services/repository/files/suggestion.go`, its handler
  `routers/web/repo/pull_review.go` `ApplySuggestion` / `applySuggestionError`, the route
  `/files/reviews/comments/{id}/apply`, and `addApplyButton` in `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`.
- **S5 (#158)** is Jack's open PR **#177** (`feat/issue-158-multiline-suggestions`).
  - It has no human approval yet.
  - It conflicts with `main` in `models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`, `comment_suggestion_test.go` and
    `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.test.ts`.
  - It adds `Comment.RangeStartLine()` and `RangeOriginalLines()`. `SuggestionOriginalLine()` returns a range's
    lines joined by `\n`.
- **S4 (#157)** has no branch or PR.

User decisions:
- **Spec reviews first.** Ask controlled-opposition now. No code on #189 or #159 until each review comment is
  posted.
- **#159 is built without S4.** The applied marking (part of AC1) and AC10 wait for S4. S4 later hooks into the
  one shared service path, so batches inherit both.
- **Stack the branches.** Fix #177's conflicts now, then `feat/issue-189-…` from #177's branch and
  `feat/issue-159-…` from #189's. Each PR merges in order after approval.

Rules: tests take expected values from the ACs, never from output. Every commit needs Jack's explicit OK, with an
`Assisted-by:` trailer and no Co-Authored-By. PRs use COURSE-WORKFLOW's format (Test Evidence, Tech Debt, AI
assistance). Log links go in issue comments only.

19	func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
20		if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
21			return optional.None[string]()
22		}
23		if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 {
24			lines, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
25			if !ok {
26				return optional.None[string]()
27			}
28			return optional.Some(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
29		}
30		patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
31		last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
32		if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
33			return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
34		}
35		return optional.Some(last[1:])
36	}
